acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether MTV-V0-007 covers the transitive dependency closure of the MCP tool path or only its own sources, and the decision is recorded.

If transitive: the guard computes go list -deps for ./internal/mcp/testvaliditybridge and fails on net, net/*, os/exec reached from the tool path, with an explicit, reviewed allowlist for any accepted standard-library edges; the current offending edges are listed with their import chains.
If direct-only stays: the spec text says so explicitly, so it is clear the transitive closure is unchecked.
body: Question, not a confirmed bug. TestToolPathImportsNoNetworkOrProcessPackage (internal/mcp/testvaliditybridge) parses only the production .go files of the bridge and internal/testvaliditydoc and rejects direct net, net/*, os/exec and unsafe syscall imports. MTV-V0-007 (docs/specs/mcp-test-validity-profile-v0.md:93-97) is worded for 'the tool path's own production sources', so the direct-only check matches its text. But the batch #1120 integrator observed on 2026-10-18 that internal/testvaliditydoc already pulls in net and os/exec through its dependencies (go list -deps), so the no-network/no-process property the requirement protects is not actually established for the MCP tool path. Also found: batch #1120 had to move #1112's external-origin parser into internal/testvaliditydoc/externalorigins after the direct-import guard caught it, so any similar helper placed one package deeper would pass unnoticed.
title: MTV-V0-007 import guard checks only direct imports; the MCP test-validity tool path already reaches net and os/exec transitively
